[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`null_resource.delete_daemonset` removes the `aws-node` (VPC CNI) DaemonSet, but it only depends on `module.eks` and `null_resource.update_kubeconfig`. It should run only after Calico has been installed via `null_resource.create_calico_installation` (Tigera operator applied and the `Installation` CR created); otherwise the order is non-deterministic and the AWS VPC CNI can be torn down before Calico takes over, leaving pods without networking. Nothing in the graph constrains delete_daemonset after the Calico install chain, so add an explicit `depends_on = [null_resource.create_calico_installation]` (no clean data reference exists for this ordering).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
`null_resource.delete_daemonset` removes the aws-node (AWS VPC CNI) daemonset from kube-system, but it only depends on `null_resource.update_kubeconfig` and `module.eks` — nothing ties it to `null_resource.create_calico_installation`. With Calico as the CNI, removing aws-node before Calico is actually installed/available leaves pods without working networking (and new nodes unable to register). The delete must be ordered after the Calico Installation is created; no attribute reference or depends_on currently expresses that.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
`:resource.null_resource.delete_daemonset` deletes the `aws-node` VPC-CNI daemonset, which is only safe once the replacement Calico CNI is actually installed by `:resource.null_resource.create_calico_installation`. The two resources share no ordering edge (both only fan in on the kubeconfig/cluster), so Terraform may delete `aws-node` first and leave nodes with no working CNI.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
`null_resource.delete_daemonset` removes the `aws-node` daemonset (disabling the AWS VPC CNI), while `null_resource.create_calico_installation` applies the Calico Installation that takes over pod networking. Both resources depend only on `null_resource.update_kubeconfig`, so Terraform may delete `aws-node` before Calico's Installation exists, leaving pods without pod networking. Calico's standard EKS install order requires deleting `aws-node` only after the Installation is applied. Since both are local-exec kubectl resources, no attribute reference can express this ordering.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
null_resource.delete_daemonset runs 'kubectl delete daemonset -n kube-system aws-node' as part of the Calico CNI migration, but it has no dependency on null_resource.create_calico_installation. Nothing in the graph orders the aws-node daemonset deletion after the Calico Installation resource is created; in a single apply these two null_resources can run concurrently, and removing aws-node before Calico is installed can break pod networking. It should depend on null_resource.create_calico_installation (bare depends_on; no data-reference fix is possible for these null_resources).
